##### SUMMARY
Always create new role

Fixes #78608
Fixes #66694 
Fixes #39543

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
```
lib/ansible/playbook/role/__init__.py
```

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
Currently the role deduplication code, primarily used for handling `allow_duplicates` always dedupes a role, preventing subsequent calls from instantiating a new instance of the role if the role uniqueness checks match.  This is fine when roles don't call other roles, but when roles do call other roles, we get some weird behaviors, with parenting and inheritance.

This PR should alleviate the "weird behaviors" while still offering a way to track role completion for `allow_duplicates` while always instantiating a new role for every use.

##### SUMMARY
The handler from a dependency role is not executed for all hosts.

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bug Report

##### COMPONENT NAME
handler

##### ANSIBLE VERSION
```
ansible 2.10.0.dev0
  config file = /etc/ansible/ansible.cfg

```
running from git checkout, `git describe` says `stable-2.9-branchpoint-1793-gec371eb227`.

##### CONFIGURATION
(no change/empty output)
##### OS / ENVIRONMENT
Arch Linux

##### STEPS TO REPRODUCE
- I have two roles that depend one one common base role
- the base role has a handler
- the roles are assigned to different hosts with `when: ...`

I am using two virtual machines provided by vagrant for this bug report but have observed the same problem on real machines in production.  You can use this Vagrant file and inventory to easy reproduction of the bug (it should reproduce with any other machine as well):

Vagrantfile:
```ruby
Vagrant.configure("2") do |config|
  ["box1", "box2"].each do |name|
    config.vm.define name do |config|
      config.vm.box = "centos/7"
    end
  end
end
```
inventory:
```ini
box1 ansible_host=127.0.0.1 ansible_port=2200 ansible_private_key_file=.vagrant/machines/box1/virtualbox/private_key
box2 ansible_host=127.0.0.1 ansible_port=2201 ansible_private_key_file=.vagrant/machines/box2/virtualbox/private_key
```

<!--- Paste example playbooks or commands between quotes below -->
```yaml
--- # playbook.yml
- hosts: all
  user: vagrant
  roles:
    - { role: role1, when: inventory_hostname == 'box1' }
    - { role: role2, when: inventory_hostname == 'box2' }
--- # roles/base/handlers/main.yml
- name: base handler
  command: echo base handler
--- # roles/base/tasks/main.yml
- command: /bin/true
--- # roles/role1/meta/main.yml
dependencies: [base]
--- # roles/role1/tasks/main.yml
- command: /bin/true
  notify: base handler
--- # roles/role2/meta/main.yml
dependencies: [base]
--- # roles/role2/tasks/main.yml
- command: /bin/true
  notify: base handler
```
##### EXPECTED RESULTS
The base handler should run on both machines.

##### ACTUAL RESULTS
It only runs on one machine:

Yes, this is expected. A couple of notes:
1. a handler in a (dependency) role inherits the `when` conditional from the role,
2. if more handlers with the same name are defined, only the last one defined is used.

See https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/user_guide/playbooks_intro.html#handlers-running-operations-on-change

However, there seems to be a bug that your example shows:
```
RUNNING HANDLER [base : base handler] ****************************************************************************
skipping: [box2]
changed: [box1]
```

should be
```
RUNNING HANDLER [base : base handler] ****************************************************************************
changed: [box2]
skipping: [box1]
```

The `base handler` handler is defined twice, once as a dependency of role1 with `when: inventory_hostname == 'box1'` and second time as dependency of role2 with `when: inventory_hostname == 'box2'`. The last one should be used, not the first one.

Leaving this open per above.
